use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the objective/goal that the C2 JU must achieve regarding assuming responsibility (R²) for Interface Units under specific correlation conditions.

evidence_cards.content: The protocols in this section are to be followed in order to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states the high-level objective (goal) for following the track correlation procedures: minimizing dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to allow automatic correlation of tracks (resolving dual designations) even when operational contingency constraints exist, provided specific ID conditions are met (Unknown/Hostile vs Friend).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level goal of the use case: resolving conflicts (dual designations) via correlation under specific exception rules.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to process two tracks for dual designation resolution after they successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the goal of processing tracks for dual designation resolution within the context of track correlation tests.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may elect to accept, automatically, changes in Environment/Category, Identity or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This paragraph defines the specific objective of resolving differences (dual designations) regarding Environment, Category, Identity, and Exercise Indicators, which constitutes the goal of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall initiate action to resolve the dual designation when it recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the objective of the use case: resolving dual designations upon recognizing track eligibility.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the goal of the use case: resolving dual designations by assuming responsibility (R²) for an Interface Unit (IU) when correlation criteria are met.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific restrictions and logic governing the correlation process, which directly constrains the objective of resolving dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The exchange of Surveillance data requires procedures to recognize and resolve differences in ID and Environment/Category.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective (goal) for resolving dual designations via track correlation: recognizing and resolving ID and Environment/Category differences during surveillance data exchange.

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to resolve dual designations when a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Directly states the objective that the primary actor (C2 JU) aims to achieve upon recognizing eligible tracks for correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to resolve dual designations by initiating the transmission of a J7.2 correlation message whenever a TN pair is determined to be a dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This text defines the primary goal and trigger for the use case: resolving dual designations via track correlation messages.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to resolve dual designations by establishing a correlation between tracks (Retained TN and Dropped TN) via J7.2 messages.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section describes the process of receiving/generating J7.2 messages to manage correlations (RV field values), which defines the goal of resolving track designations.

evidence_cards.content: PPLI data available from J2 messages shall be used by C² JUs to reduce the redundancy of surveillance track reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that PPLI data availability is a prerequisite condition for the C² JU to begin correlation and conflict processing to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: A surveillance JU will accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and perform the applicable correlation and conflict processing necessary to ensure that duplicative information is not being transmitted on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state requirement: the surveillance JU must have accepted PPLI data into its database before it can perform correlation — a necessary precondition for resolving dual designations via track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.

source_locations.location: paragraph under 4.4.4.3.1 AIR AND SURFACE TRACK CORRELATION

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system capability that must be present before the use case (resolving dual designations via track correlation) can begin; without this capability, the process cannot commence.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.

source_locations.location: Section g. Correlation Restrictions, paragraphs (1) through (4)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These restrictions define mandatory preconditions that must NOT hold for automatic correlation to proceed — thus establishing boundary conditions under which the use case cannot begin or must be inhibited unless overridden by operator capability.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction on ID conflict (paragraph 4.4.4.3.1i), subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C2 IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that while certain preconditions normally block automatic correlation, they can be overridden via configured system parameters — implying that precondition state may be modifiable before use case initiation.

evidence_cards.content: In lieu of specific interface direction, all IUs will restrict automatic correlation by default.

source_locations.location: Section g.(1) and g.(2), closing parenthetical statements

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the default system state prior to any override — indicating that without explicit configuration or communication, the precondition for blocking automatic correlation is active.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is the subject of a current engagement status message; i.e., the TN is the same TN appearing in a J10.2 Engagement Status message Target TN or Reference TN field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This operational contingency constraint (OCC) must hold before correlation can be restricted or allowed under specific exceptions, thus it serves as a precondition for resolving dual designations via track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message originated by or addressed to own unit or a J12.0 Mission Assignment message originated by own unit for which a reply is required and has not been transmitted or received.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This OCC represents a system state that must exist prior to initiating correlation resolution, making it a valid precondition for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is currently a controlled track, i.e., a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message has been transmitted or received.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Controlled track status is an operational contingency constraint that must be satisfied before correlation actions are evaluated — hence a precondition.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is an active or inactive IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: IU status (active/inactive) is listed as an operational contingency constraint affecting correlation eligibility — therefore a precondition for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Either track is currently the subject of a dual designation resolution action involving another TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states a condition under which tracks are already engaged in resolution — a necessary pre-state before this use case can proceed on those tracks.

evidence_cards.content: One track is a common local track and the other is a remote, and the same unit has R² for both tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a structural relationship between tracks and ownership (R²) that must hold before correlation logic applies — thus a foundational precondition.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks must pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state (passing tests twice) required before the correlation process can begin.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they are deemed a tentative correlation and shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an intermediate precondition state (tentative correlation) that precedes full execution.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have the capability to transmit and receive all response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks that are held locally by its system.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a mandatory system capability (precondition) required before the C2 JU can participate in resolving dual designations via track correlation using J7.2 messages.

evidence_cards.content: A TN pair has been determined to be a dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the specific system state that must exist before the C2 JU can initiate the correlation message transmission (the start of the use case).

evidence_cards.content: The originating C2 JU holds R² for the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This condition regarding track responsibility is required for the subsequent action of dropping the TN and transmitting the J7.0 message, which is part of the resolution process described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have received or generated a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 for automatic acceptance of the requested correlation to be considered.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the system state (RV field = 3 in J7.2 message) that must hold before the use case can proceed under automatic acceptance mode — a direct precondition for this variant of the correlation resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: For manual correlation requests that are rejected, the JU originating the request must provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination — implying that if no such alert is configured or available, the manual correlation rejection path cannot complete successfully without human intervention.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: While not strictly a precondition for starting the use case, it defines a required system capability (operator alert provision) that must be present for the manual correlation rejection branch to function as specified — thus acting as a conditional precondition for successful handling of rejected manual correlations.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must be holding the Dropped TN for the correlation request to be processed under the specific conditions outlined in section g.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a state requirement (holding the Dropped TN) necessary for the specific processing logic described in the document to apply.

evidence_cards.content: If the C2 JU is not holding the Dropped TN, it shall not take any further action regarding the correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a negative precondition or constraint: absence of the Dropped TN prevents the use case from proceeding.

evidence_cards.content: A C2 JU participating on the Surveillance Network PG shall attempt to correlate received PPLI reports with data being received from local sensors.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the primary action initiating the main flow: the system actively attempts correlation between incoming PPLI and local sensor data.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R2, the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific step for resolving dual designations where the actor owns the track: transmitting the J7.2 message with specific field values (RV=1, Retained/Dropped TNs).

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Completes the resolution sequence by specifying the follow-up actions (ceasing reporting and sending Drop Track) after the correlation message is sent.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first step of the main flow: the recognition of eligibility and the initiation of resolution action (automatic or manual).

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific system action (transmitting the J7.2 message) taken by the primary actor to execute the resolution.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the critical content/payload of the main flow interaction (identifying Retained vs Dropped tracks).

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the standard system response (acceptance) in the main flow, while noting the existence of exception paths.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a TN pair is determined to be a dual designation, the recognizing JU shall initiate transmission of the J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN selection in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1j.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action step for resolving the dual designation by transmitting the correlation message.

evidence_cards.content: The RV field in the J7.2 message shall be set to 0 if there is no OCC on the Retained TN, 1 if the Retained TN has an OCC, or 3 if the correlation was manually initiated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the data constraints and parameter settings required during the transmission of the correlation message.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a conditional follow-up action within the main flow regarding the dropping of the track and sending a specific termination message.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU receives or generates a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection), it shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system's response and constraint in the main flow following a correlation rejection event (RV=2).

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation (RV=2), the originating JU shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory actor action required in the main flow when a manual correlation is rejected.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3, the C2 JU shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless specific restrictions apply (different E/C, simulated vs live tracks, or both locally derived real-time tracks).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the successful automatic acceptance step in the main flow for RV=3 messages, including the conditions under which this success path is blocked.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs rejecting the requested correlation shall initiate transmission of a J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN set as received and RV field set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary actor's action in the main flow when rejecting a correlation request — part of the canonical success scenario for resolving dual designations via track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path (reverse correlation) within the main interaction sequence, specifying how the C2 JU modifies track numbers and sets RV=1 to complete correlation successfully.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN has an OCC, then if RV is set to 0, transmit a reverse correlation with RV set to 1; if RV is set to 1, transmit a correlation rejection with RV set to 2; if RV is set to 3, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies conditional actions under a variant state (Retained TN not held), including both successful outcomes (reverse correlation or direct execution) that constitute valid completions of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: If the Dropped TN does not have an OCC, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines another successful completion path under specific data conditions (no OCC on Dropped TN), contributing to the canonical success scenario by showing how correlation proceeds without OCC dependency.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative successful path where the C² JU does not hold R² but still resolves dual designation by transmitting a J7.2 message with RV=1, diverging from the main flow step where the recognizing JU holds R² and sets RV based on OCC or manual initiation.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative successful path where no J7.2 message is transmitted because TNs are identical; instead, the system accepts PPLI data and suppresses redundant J3 reporting — a divergence from the main flow’s requirement to transmit J7.2 and establish Retained/Dropped TN correlation.

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a) if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend; automatic correlation may be allowed with the Unknown/Hostile track becoming the dropped Track Number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This paragraph defines a specific legal alternative path (exception) that allows automatic correlation under conditions where it would normally be restricted, diverging from the standard correlation restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: If the RV field is set to value 0 in the J7.2 message, it indicates that a reverse correlation request would be acceptable.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path where the receiving IU can propose a reverse correlation (swapping Retained/Dropped TNs) instead of simply accepting or rejecting the original request.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative success path for manually initiated correlations, distinguishing them from automatic ones regarding acceptance criteria.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific variant of the main flow where the originating unit performs an additional action (dropping the track locally) based on its responsibility status.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs capable of transmitting the J7.2 message shall have an operator selectable capability to deactivate automatic transmission of the message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative path where the standard automatic initiation is suppressed by operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU receives or generates a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection), it shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow behavior where correlation is rejected but the system suppresses automatic retry attempts for a defined time window, diverging from the main flow's successful correlation establishment.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative path triggered by manual correlation rejection, requiring human intervention via voice coordination instead of automated resolution.

evidence_cards.content: An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This indicates that for automatic correlation rejections, operator alerting is optional — representing a configurable variant of the alternative flow.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful flow (automatic acceptance under RV=3) that diverges from the standard automatic correlation logic, contingent on specific track compatibility conditions.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN has an OCC: (a) if RV=0, transmit reverse correlation with RV=1; (b) if RV=1, transmit correlation rejection with RV=2; (c) if RV=3, execute correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines alternative successful paths when the initiating unit does not hold the Retained TN — a divergence from main flow step 5 (transmit J7.2 requesting correlation), resulting in different message types or execution logic based on RV value.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN does not have an OCC, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Alternative path diverging from main flow step 5 — instead of transmitting a J7.2 request, the unit directly executes correlation locally under specific conditions (no OCC on Dropped TN).

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs rejecting the requested correlation shall initiate transmission of a J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN set as received and RV field set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Alternative flow branch where receiving unit rejects correlation — still results in successful resolution via explicit rejection signaling (RV=2), diverging from main flow’s acceptance/execution path.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Alternative successful outcome where receiver proposes swapped roles (reverse correlation) — diverges from main flow by altering TN assignment while maintaining correlation intent (RV=1).

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs not holding the Dropped TN shall not take any further action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Alternative terminal state for units that cannot participate in correlation due to lack of Dropped TN — represents a valid non-action path within the protocol, avoiding invalid operations.

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a) above: If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This text defines a specific legal alternative path for resolving dual designations that overrides standard operational contingency constraints (OCCs), satisfying the 'alternative_flow' slot requirement for diverging paths.

evidence_cards.content: Under this exception, the Unknown/Hostile track shall be the dropped Track Number (TN-2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the mandatory outcome (Retained/Dropped assignment) for the alternative flow, distinguishing it from the main flow where selection logic might differ.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative flow where the operator resolves an ID conflict via alert-driven manual intervention, diverging from the standard automatic correlation path when this specific restriction exists.

evidence_cards.content: If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a mandatory alternative flow step (decorrelation testing) that must occur after conflict resolution but before correlation execution.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception flow condition (timeout) and the resulting system response (cancellation).

evidence_cards.content: If own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific variant of the alternative flow regarding the disposition of the Dropped Track Number based on ownership status.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit has R^2 for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted for the Dropped TN. If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0, own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details an alternative flow path involving dropping a track when the unit has responsibility (R^2), including handling subsequent reports and a retry inhibition timer.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message which own unit originated or to which own unit is preparing a reply, the system shall execute the decorrelation and provide operator display of new track status on TNs A and B before release of the J9.0 reply; the reply shall be relative to TN A only.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path for resolving dual designations when a specific command message state exists, diverging from standard automatic processing by requiring immediate execution and display updates prior to message release.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message), the system shall not automatically decorrelate; if manually decorrelated, it alerts the operator to report termination of control TN A if appropriate, and reports commencement of control of TN B using the J10.5 message only if initiated by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path where automatic correlation is inhibited due to control status, shifting the resolution process to manual operator initiation with specific reporting constraints.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of a J10.6 message), the system shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path for handling dual designations involving paired tracks, requiring operator intervention to manage the pairing transfer rather than standard correlation logic.

evidence_cards.content: When Local Data is PENDING and Remote Data is HOSTILE (or vice versa), the system issues an Operator Alert (1*), but systems may have a feature to automatically accept the received ID as the local ID.

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-2, cells at intersection of PENDING/HOSTILE and UNKNOWN/HOSTILE rows/columns; Legend note '*'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific alternative flow for conflicting IDs where automatic correlation is permitted under specific conditions (Unknown/Hostile vs Friend/Pending) rather than requiring manual intervention.

evidence_cards.content: If Local Data is FRIEND and Remote Data is NEUTRAL (or SUSPECT or HOSTILE), the system automatically accepts the received ID as the LOCAL ID (Action 2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides evidence for the variant dimension mentioned in the goal scope regarding automatic correlation of tracks when specific ID conditions (Friend vs others) are met.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow path where automatic correlation is halted due to conflicting operational contingency constraints (OCCs) on both tracks, diverging from the main flow of immediate J7.2 transmission.

evidence_cards.content: Transmission of a J7.2 message with RV field set to 0 or 1 shall be discontinued upon receipt of a J7.2 message containing one or both of the same TNs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative flow triggered by receiving a competing correlation request, causing the originating C2 JU to stop its own transmission — a divergence from the main flow’s uninterrupted transmission sequence.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path where correlation is rejected but system suppresses automatic retry for a defined time window — a valid divergence from main flow that still allows eventual resolution via manual coordination.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies human-in-the-loop recovery behavior following rejection — an alternative successful path diverging from automatic correlation main flow, enabling resolution via voice coordination.

evidence_cards.content: An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates configurable alternative response to automatic correlation rejection — supports variant paths where operator intervention may or may not be triggered, affecting how the system proceeds after divergence.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) different E/C or existing E/C conflict; (2) one track simulated and other live; (3) both tracks locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines mandatory acceptance under RV=3 (manual initiation) except when specific structural conflicts exist — represents an alternative flow branch where correlation succeeds despite prior rejections or OCCs, provided no hard constraints block it.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes post-alternative-flow stabilization rule — ensures manually resolved correlations are protected from immediate reversal, supporting continuity of the alternative success path.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception handling path where the system must discard the incoming PPLI message instead of the local surveillance track based on the Geodetic Position Quality field being 0.

evidence_cards.content: Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a hard constraint/exception that prevents correlation processing entirely for subsurface tracks involving IUs.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled) shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a terminal exception outcome where correlation is rejected upon receipt of a J7.2 message if operational contingency constraints (OCCs) are held on both tracks or if conflicting IDs exist and the ID conflict restriction is enabled.

evidence_cards.content: The exception allowing automatic correlation despite an engagement status message (when one track is Unknown/Hostile and the other is Friend) shall not be applied by any JU upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that even when an ID-based exception condition exists, the presence of a received J7.2 Correlation message prevents application of that exception, forcing rejection behavior instead.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the timeout condition that triggers the exception flow for the 'Resolve Dual Designations' use case.

evidence_cards.content: If the correlation fails due to the 60-second timeout, all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system response and terminal state (cancellation) when the correlation exception occurs.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 2 in a J7.2 message, it indicates that the correlation request has been rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the explicit system response for rejecting a correlation request, which constitutes an exception flow outcome where the dual designation resolution fails.

evidence_cards.content: The originating JU can indicate in the J7.2 message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation by setting the Response Value (RV) field to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a condition under which the normal negotiation path (reverse correlation) is blocked, representing an exception handling mechanism for constraints on the originating unit.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (OCC conflict on both tracks) that prevents successful correlation initiation and mandates abandonment of the attempt.

evidence_cards.content: Transmission of a J7.2 message with RV field set to 0 or 1 shall be discontinued upon receipt of a J7.2 message containing one or both of the same TNs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception handling path where automatic correlation transmission is terminated due to competing correlation activity from another unit.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV field set to 0 or 1 shall not accept the requested correlation when local or remote data indicates a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g; in this case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception flow for receiving units: rejection of correlation request due to pre-existing restrictions, preventing successful completion of the use case from the receiver’s perspective.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be rejected if the Retained TN and the Dropped TN decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition (decorrelation) that causes the correlation process to fail/terminate.

evidence_cards.content: If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC (Operational Contingency Constraint), the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a conflict state where both tracks are constrained, resulting in rejection.

evidence_cards.content: If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a rejection path based on the combination of an OCC on the dropped track and a specific message value (RV=1).

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C or either has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks. In these cases, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Lists specific data conflicts (E/C, Live/Simulated, Locally Derived) that override automatic acceptance (RV=3) and force rejection.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs rejecting the requested correlation shall initiate transmission of a J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN set as received and RV field set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception handling path when a C2 JU rejects a correlation request — specifying both the trigger (rejection) and required system response (J7.2 message with RV=2).

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative exception flow where instead of rejecting, the unit performs a reverse correlation — altering track roles and setting RV=1 as part of error recovery or negotiation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs not holding the Dropped TN shall not take any further action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a terminal exception outcome: if the receiving unit does not hold the Dropped TN, it takes no action — effectively halting processing for that correlation attempt.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, the correlation request shall be processed conditionally based on whether the Dropped TN has an OCC and the current RV value.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a complex exception branch triggered by asymmetric track ownership — leading to sub-paths (g(1)(a)-(c), g(2)) that define how the system responds under partial data availability.

evidence_cards.content: If RV is set to 0, transmit a reverse correlation with RV set to 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Exception sub-flow: when Dropped TN has OCC and RV=0, system must respond with reverse correlation (RV=1) — indicating a negotiated retry or role swap.

evidence_cards.content: If RV is set to 1, transmit a correlation rejection with RV set to 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Exception sub-flow: when Dropped TN has OCC and RV=1, system must reject correlation (RV=2) — escalating to explicit rejection after prior reverse attempt.

evidence_cards.content: If RV is set to 3, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Exception sub-flow: when RV=3 (manual initiation), system proceeds with correlation despite missing Retained TN — overriding normal constraints.

evidence_cards.content: If the Dropped TN does not have an OCC, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Exception sub-flow: bypasses OCC check and executes correlation directly — simplifying resolution when operational contingency is absent.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs rejecting a J7.2 message and holding the Dropped TN as a local or common local track shall not interpret the J7.2 message as a Drop Track message for the purpose of determining R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies exception behavior: rejection does not imply drop intent — preserving responsibility state (R²) even during failed correlation attempts.

evidence_cards.content: If the received J7.2 message contains one or both of the same TNs as contained in the transmission of the own unit J7.2 message sequence in progress, specific actions shall be taken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a collision/overlap exception condition — triggering special handling when concurrent correlation sequences involve overlapping TNs.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-correlation system state for track designation when the Dropped TN is held locally — a direct observable outcome after successful correlation completion.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted for the Dropped TN; if the Dropped TN is later reported by another IU, own unit shall retain it as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate with the Retained TN for 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the post-correlation system behavior regarding track retention and suppression of re-correlation attempts — an observable state change following successful correlation execution.

evidence_cards.content: When a J7.2 message is initiated by own unit and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, it shall be retained as a remote track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state regarding the Dropped TN immediately after correlation initiation but before drop confirmation, which is part of the post-correlation condition.

evidence_cards.content: Data specified below shall be transferred from the Dropped TN to the Retained TN when the correlation is executed: Kinematic Data (Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, Strength), Identification Data (ID/IAD, Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type - subject to conflict restrictions), and IFF/SIF Data (nonzero modes where Retained TN data is zero).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact data attributes that are merged into the Retained TN upon successful execution of the correlation, defining the resulting system state.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful completion of the correlation, if the originating C² JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after transmitting the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an immediate system state change post-successful correlation: dropping the track and sending a specific deactivation message when ownership conditions are met.

evidence_cards.content: Transmission of a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall be discontinued upon receipt of a J7.2 message containing one or both of the same TNs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: While this describes termination of transmission under competing requests, it implies that in the absence of such conflict (i.e., successful path), the transmission completes and is not discontinued — supporting the notion of stable post-correlation state.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV=3), the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific system state constraint (stabilization period) that exists immediately after the successful completion of the use case when performed manually.
